claims.text: The target material is bulk, polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed model applies to both oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr and HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The GNN will be trained using experimental and theoretical thermal- and electrical-conductivity data for HfNbTaTiZr.
The GNN can predict the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The GNN can predict the electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The GNN will be more accurate than existing analytical approaches.
The expected accuracy advantage applies especially over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Atomic arrangement and bonding are the structural information mediating the conductivity predictions.
The GNN learns relationships among atomic structure, temperature, and conductivity.
Learning those relationships enables more accurate conductivity predictions.
The predicted thermal-conductivity MAE is less than 0.5 W m^-1 K^-1.
The predicted electrical-conductivity MAE is less than 1×10^-6 S m^-1.
The Boltzmann transport equation is an example of the existing analytical baseline.
The model's stated applicability is limited to bulk, polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr, with or without 1 wt.% oxygen, over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Model accuracy may be limited by the quality and quantity of the training data.
The model may not generalize to other temperature regimes or sample conditions.
Evaluation will use a held-out subset that is separate from the training subset.
A held-out thermal-conductivity MAE exceeding 1.0 W m^-1 K^-1 will falsify the hypothesis.
A held-out electrical-conductivity MAE exceeding 2×10^-6 S m^-1 will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted MAEs are below 0.5 W m^-1 K^-1 and 1×10^-6 S m^-1, but falsification is triggered only above 1.0 W m^-1 K^-1 and 2×10^-6 S m^-1. Results between those thresholds would violate the stated prediction without falsifying it.
The outcome is framed as improved accuracy relative to analytical approaches, but no baseline MAE or same-benchmark comparison against an analytical method is specified in the held-out design.
